title: Latency Anchors & Gatekeeper: soft quotas for geo-pin and capacity-aware shedding
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a combined 'latency anchors' + 'gatekeeper' routing policy to improve SLO adherence during multi-region capacity pressure. This ticket designs and implements: 1) latency-anchor scoring to prefer region candidates whose p50/p95 are within configured SLO windows; 2) a gatekeeper layer that enforces soft capacity quotas per region (tokenized credits) and transitions traffic to fallback regions or degrade path when soft quota is exhausted; 3) circuit-breaker escalation rules that open/close per-region paths based on sustained latency and error-rate signals; and 4) integration with existing KV cache-awareness so pinned requests retain affinity where possible. Goal: reduce p95 SLO breaches for enterprise customers during bursty traffic while keeping unit-cost impact predictable.
acceptance_criteria: Latency-anchor score computed per request using last 10s/1m p50/p95 and request weight
Gatekeeper issues soft quota tokens per region and emits metrics for spent/remaining tokens
When soft quota depleted, policy migrates fraction of traffic (configurable) to fallback regions with higher cost but available capacity
Circuit-breaker trips if region p95 > configured threshold for 120s and error rate > 3% for that window
End-to-end tests show <10% reduction in p95 SLO breaches under synthetic multi-region overload compared to baseline
Dashboard and alerting: new per-region gatekeeper metrics + SLO burn rate panel in Console
tasks: Spec latency-anchor scoring formula and default thresholds
Prototype gatekeeper token bucket and soft-quota enforcement in steerer service
Add circuit-breaker state machine and durable state storage for cross-restart resilience
Integrate gatekeeper decisions with request router and KV-cache metadata
Create canary regression tests using chaos traffic generator (region overload scenarios)
Instrument metrics and dashboards; add unit/integration tests
Submit RFC and get cross-team review (SRE, Runtime, Console)

notes: Trade-offs: favoring latency anchors preserves user-perceived latency but may increase inter-region egress costs when fallback is used. Gatekeeper soft quotas aim to balance cost vs SLOs; hard quotas avoided to prevent wholesale outage.

Operational runbook: include steps to force-disable gatekeeper for a region, to drain tokens, and to revert to round-robin fallback in emergency. Add runbook link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Runbooks/Gatekeeper+Runbook
Observability plan: emit gatekeeper.token_grant, gatekeeper.token_spend, latency_anchor.score, cb.state_change, region_migration.event to Console metrics and traces
